title: PPGNN: Fast and Accurate Privacy-Preserving Graph Neural Network Inference via Parallel and Pipelined Arithmetic-and-Logic FHE Accelerator
problem: Existing privacy-preserving GNN inference schemes using Fully Homomorphic Encryption suffer from high computational overhead, accuracy degradation, or incomplete data protection when ensuring graph structure confidentiality and maintaining computation precision.
motivation: Cloud-based GNN inference services increasingly process sensitive data in applications like social media and bioinformatics, making data privacy critical.
method: PPGNN runs neural networks on encrypted graphs using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) — a technique that lets computers do arithmetic and logical operations directly on encrypted data without decrypting it. To keep computation practical, the system uses smaller encryption parameters, which reduces the amount of processing needed. A custom hardware accelerator with specialized units performs these encrypted operations in a pipelined fashion — like an assembly line where different processing stages handle different calculations simultaneously — enabling multiple operations to run in parallel.
key_novelty: Combining smaller-parameter arithmetic-and-logic fully homomorphic encryption with specialized pipelined hardware acceleration enables parallel privacy-preserving graph neural network inference.
contributions: Novel high-accuracy arithmetic-and-logic FHE algorithm for GNN inference with substantially reduced parameter requirements
Dedicated hardware architecture with specialized FHE operation units and pipelined implementation
Achieves 2.7× speedup over Arithmetic FHE accelerators and 1.5× over Logic FHE accelerators
Delivers approximately 18× average energy reduction compared to state-of-the-art approaches

metrics.speedup: 2.7× vs Arithmetic FHE, 1.5× vs Logic FHE

primary_theme: Privacy-preserving GNN inference via pipelined FHE accelerator
